DEWATERING

Groundwater Information: What to Assemble Before Seeking a Proposal

Make the uncertainty visible so the specialist can ask the right questions.

In this insight

Collect the existing evidenceConnect water information to the excavationUse an information-gap registerPreserve assumptions in the commercial recordFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Collect the existing evidence

Start with the available geotechnical reports, borehole information, groundwater observations and relevant site history. Include dates and locations so readers can understand the context of each observation. A single recorded level should not be presented as a complete description of site behaviour. Ask the responsible specialists to identify whether the information is sufficient for the decision being made.

Connect water information to the excavation

Provide proposed levels, staging, retaining arrangements and the intended permanent structure. Water-management questions cannot be understood in isolation from the work they support. Identify nearby assets and known environmental or discharge constraints that may require assessment. The enquiry should bring these inputs together instead of requiring the bidder to reconstruct the project from unrelated documents.

Use an information-gap register

Record missing data, the person responsible for obtaining it and the decision that depends on it. Prioritise gaps that prevent a meaningful option comparison or create major uncertainty in the commercial offer. Where additional investigation is proposed, obtain a clear explanation of its purpose. This helps the client distinguish a useful decision-enabling task from an unexplained request for more information.

Preserve assumptions in the commercial record

If a preliminary proposal must proceed before all information is available, list the assumptions and the review triggers. Update the proposal when new evidence arrives. Avoid allowing a feasibility estimate to become a fixed expectation after its original basis has changed. A transparent information trail supports better decisions and a fairer discussion of scope, programme and price as the project develops.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Retain dates and locations for observations.
  • Link groundwater information to excavation stages.
  • Track assumptions until the required evidence is available.

References & further reading

  • Further reading: USACE — Dewatering methods and performance monitoring, historical technical guidance

International references provide technical context; applicable local requirements and the project engineer’s decisions govern the actual works.
